content:
jessica_h: heads up — noticed a staging latency spike ~5m ago. looks correlated with a big batched job from tenant `acme-staging`. anyone on? :eyes:
ops-bot: Alert: staging-pool-warm-1 90th/99th latency crossed thresholds (p90=1.6s, p99=2.8s). source_hint=pool-warm-1
raj_patel: can you paste the tail of the worker logs and the slice id? also any recent config changes?
jessica_h: slice id `warm-1-az2-233`. tail:```INFO 12:34:56 kv_cache_miss_rate=93%
WARN 12:34:57 preemptions=4
ERROR 12:34:58 evict_reason=spillback
DEBUG 12:34:59 concurrent_batches=30
```
elliot_m: kv cache thrash + 30 concurrent batched requests = classic churn. were they sending long contexts?
jessica_h: yes, lots of ~2000 token payloads in a single request, and many of them had overlapping prefixes. warm pool prefetched KV for first requests, then evicted when bursts kept adding new prefix state.
kevin_z: thoughts: short-term we can either route heavy-batch requests to a small reserved slice or apply per-tenant batch concurrency admission control. tradeoffs: routing => reserved capacity cost; admission control => client throttling / degraded UX.
raj_patel: do we have any spare fractional slices we can use cheaply (preemptible)?
elliot_m: we have preemptible spare in eu-west warm pool but NIC/PCIe could still saturate if they keep parallelism. NIC shaping + cache TTL bump might help too.
jessica_h: proposal: immediate action = soft per-tenant batch cap 8 + route overflow to reserve-flow-3 (lower SLO). medium = tag-based routing and NIC egress shaping for heavy-batch tenants.
kevin_z: i'll spin up a soft-cap prototype: `max_batch_concurrency_per_tenant=8` + `overflow_route=reserve-flow-3`. can we A/B on staging 10% first? @ops-bot canary please. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Canary created — routing rule applied for tenant `acme-staging`: 10% -> reserve-flow-3 with soft_cap=8. Monitoring window 15m.
jessica_h: i'll monitor p90/p99 + kv-miss dashboards and share graphs. if good, we push to 100% and add to routing policy.
raj_patel: also add cost check — if reserve-flow uses preemptible GPUs cost should be small, but capture delta in INFRA spend dashboard.
elliot_m: add one more metric to alerts: kv_cache_miss_rate > 60% should trigger a different paging threshold (so we detect cache churn vs network errors).
jessica_h: filed INFRA-4523 with logs, actions, and a follow-up to update alerting thresholds and docs. thanks all.
kevin_z: nice. once canary finishes i'll run a quick perf sweep and post results.
jessica_h: closing loop here in ~20m after canary completes. :wave:
